clue.text: Quote father about distant ancestor

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the two pieces together are read backwards as one run

parts.note: to quote someone is to name or cite them
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Someone cites their dad on the subject of early human forebears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the whole run NAMEPA backwards to give AP EMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A primitive hominid imagined as the link between apes and humans is a remote forebear of ours.

clue.text: Look by waterfall for fliers

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance
force is a northern English word for a waterfall

explanation.surface: Someone peers across a cascade at birds or pilots.
explanation.walkthrough: FORCE for a waterfall is from the dialect of the English Lake District and north.
explanation.definitionFit: An air force is a nation's military aviators collectively.

clue.text: A girdle in Puck's line

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream, Puck boasts he will put a girdle round about the earth; the clue wants the imaginary belt round the globe

explanation.surface: A belt mentioned in a line spoken by Shakespeare's mischievous sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: Puck says 'I'll put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes'; 'line' means a line of verse but also a line on the map.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary circle around the middle of the Earth is like a belt about the planet.

clue.text: Peri had to represent this goddess

indicators.note: represent here is re-present, to show again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fairy has to play the part of a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represent' rearranges PERIHADTO. A peri is a fairy in Persian myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of love and beauty, counterpart of Venus, is the goddess meant.

clue.text: True Londoners have to listen out for them on arrival

definitions.text: True Londoners have to listen out for them on arrival

parts.words: True Londoners have to listen out for them on arrival
parts.note: a true Cockney is said to be born within earshot of the peal of a particular East London church, so a newborn hears them on arriving in the world

explanation.surface: Proper Londoners must keep their ears open for something when they turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On arrival' sounds like arriving in town, but it means being born: a Cockney, the traditional East End Londoner, is by legend born within the sound of the bells of St Mary-le-Bow church.
explanation.definitionFit: The bells of St Mary-le-Bow define who counts as a Cockney, so true Londoners must hear them at birth.

clue.text: What could make couple so mixed up (mum's heart being lost)?

definitions.text: What could make couple so mixed up (mum's heart being lost)?

indicators.note: the letters given could be made into the answer, so they are to be rearranged
being lost says one letter drops out of the words before it
the heart of mum is its central letter

explanation.surface: What might leave a couple so confused, with a mother's love gone astray?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could make' rearranges COUPLESOMIXEDUP after 'being lost' removes U, the heart of 'mum'. Read whole, the clue describes Freud's son fixated on his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud's term for a child's desire for the opposite-sex parent tangles mother and son in exactly this way.

clue.text: He's prejudiced in a grand manner against books

parts.note: to talk big is to speak in a grand or boastful manner
OT, the Old Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: A man shows grand-scale bias against literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' just places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot is an intolerant person, someone narrow-minded who is biased against others.

clue.text: Lion's starting to consume the woman's skin

indicators.note: the starting letter of the word lion

parts.note: to eat is to consume
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A lion begins devouring a woman's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is animal hide that has been tanned.

clue.text: Several star on Doctor Finlay in the end

parts.note: the sun is a star

indicators.note: in the end picks only the closing letter of the name Finlay

explanation.surface: A celebrity appears on a vintage medical drama, eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Finlay is the hero of Dr Finlay's Casebook, a long-running BBC drama about a Scottish country doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundry means various or miscellaneous, a number of different things.

clue.text: Each art critic's reviewed feature

indicators.note: reviewed here means looked over again and re-ordered, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Each art reviewer's critiqued article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges EACHARTCRITICS, keeping the S of 'critic's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic is a distinguishing trait or quality.

clue.text: Hooligans take note back, getting extra purchase

parts.note: roughs are rowdy thugs, hooligans

indicators.note: back says the word for the note is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Thugs grab a banknote and get something extra for their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DOH into HOD. 'Note' suggests a banknote and 'purchase' buying, but purchase here means grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse shod roughshod has nails sticking out of its shoes to stop it slipping, so it gets a better grip.

clue.text: Corn needs a little good watering from above

indicators.note: a little of the word good is just its opening letter

parts.note: rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A cereal crop needs some decent irrigation by sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is cereal crops in general, which are grown for their edible seeds, the grain.

clue.text: Odour to dodge in the countryside

indicators.note: a dodge is a trick or move, so these letters swerve into a new order

explanation.surface: A bad smell to avoid out in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodge' rearranges ODOURTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of doors, in the open air, is what being in the countryside means here.

clue.text: Thrower of clay pot

definitions.meaning: in baseball the player who throws the ball to the batter
a large earthenware jug for pouring liquids

explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrower of clay' looks like a potter at the wheel, but 'of' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the baseball player who throws and an earthenware jug for liquids.

clue.text: My soldier's dog

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
GI is an American soldier; the 's means 'has' here

explanation.surface: A serviceman's pet hound is described.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small short-legged Welsh breed of dog.

clue.text: Woollen fabric is ready by length, saving a bit of time

parts.note: ready money, or 'the readies', is cash

indicators.note: saving here means except for, so one letter is left out of the word for the length

parts.note: a metre is a unit of length

indicators.note: a bit of the word time is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A soft material is prepared at speed, according to its length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' means 'except', removing T (a bit of 'time') from METRE to leave MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, made into cloth.

clue.text: See me about to give boy weapon that's jammed?

indicators.note: about here means around, so the word me goes round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
to arm a lad is to give a boy a weapon

explanation.surface: Come to me about arming a youngster with something that is stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link, an instruction to look at the wordplay. 'about' puts ME around ARM A LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a preserve, a citrus jam, so the question mark fits something made into jam.

clue.text: Mostly strict, say, reformed church division

indicators.note: reformed means formed anew, so the letters are rearranged
mostly says the word strict loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A fairly rigid, perhaps Reformation-era, split in the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' cuts STRICT to STRIC; 'reformed' rearranges that with SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacristy is a room in a church where vestments and sacred vessels are kept, a part of the building.

clue.text: Closest friend not quite changed by success

indicators.note: not quite says the word for changed loses its last letter

parts.note: altered means changed
to make a go of something is to make a success of it

explanation.surface: A best mate who has almost changed after doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts the D off ALTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego, literally 'other self', is used for a trusted intimate companion.

clue.text: Love performing in support of light satire

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces that support another sit beneath it

parts.note: a lamp is a light
love is zero in tennis, written O
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Love, acted on behalf of comic mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in support of' puts O and ON underneath LAMP in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampoon is a piece of ridicule, a mocking attack in writing.

clue.text: Wild revel's cut short by agreement to German wine

indicators.note: cut short says the word for the revel loses its last letter

parts.note: a riot is a wild revel; the 's means 'is'
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A rowdy party is curtailed once Germans agree on a vintage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the T from RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish vintage from the region of that name.

clue.text: The porridge maker has nothing at breakfast, perhaps

parts.note: O, zero, is nothing
breakfast is one example of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone making porridge eats nothing at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats are what porridge is made from.

clue.text: A little wasp I got with a tap

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone swatted a small wasp with a light blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'with a tap' cannot replace a noun; 'with' is a link and 'tap' the definition. 'A little' hides the answer in 'wasp I got'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a peg or tap for drawing liquid from a cask.

clue.text: Old city ceremony seen by English couple in Rome once

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An ancient town's rites are watched by an English pair in old Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was a Roman town buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, an ancient settlement.

clue.text: Follow to make certain right away

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain

explanation.surface: Someone is told to follow instructions so as to be sure immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once', but it splits: R (right) goes away from ENSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after or result.

clue.text: Added text to change book

parts.note: a PS, postscript, is text added at the end of a letter
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: Someone inserts words to alter a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a volume containing the Psalms.

clue.text: Nothing in the gallery is merchandise

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the word for the theatre balcony

parts.note: the gods is the top gallery of a theatre
O, the round figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: An empty theatre balcony is on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods is the highest balcony of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods are articles for sale, the stock a trader deals in.

clue.text: Who might be eager to be done with nest?

definitions.text: Who might be eager to be done with nest?

indicators.note: done is used here as worked over, so the letters of the two words are refashioned

explanation.surface: Who could be keen to leave home at last?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be done' rearranges EAGER and NEST together; the whole clue also describes youngsters impatient to fly the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescents are the ones itching to leave the parental home and strike out alone.

clue.text: A number refuse to keep Conservative in political faction

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: to keep means the word for refuse holds another piece inside it

parts.note: to deny is to refuse

explanation.surface: Several decline to retain a Tory within their party grouping.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics a 'tendency' is a faction within a party, as in the Militant Tendency of the 1980s Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency is a group within a larger political party pursuing its own line.

clue.text: Race without proper start is run again

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the race goes around another piece

parts.note: a relay is a race run by teams

indicators.note: the start of proper is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A race lacking a fair start has to be rerun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: RELAY goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a match or race contested a second time.
